messages:
harry: Heads-up — noticed a spike in audit-export latency around 14:20 UTC. Sampling TTLs got reduced in prod yesterday and S3 uploader is falling behind. Some GPU nodes are stuck in 'waiting-for-logs' during boot because disk-scheduler blocks while exporter backlog drains.
maya: ugh. is this the `audit.sampling.ttl` change from the rollout?
harry: yeah, @maya rolled that canary in eu-west-1 yesterday afternoon. TTL set from 72h -> 12h to reduce storage costs, but the exporter assumed linear throughput. Now we have bursts and the uploader queue grows.
liam: how many nodes affected? are GPU pools failing join or just delayed warmup?
harry: mostly warmup delays. ~35 nodes across eu-west-1 and ap-north. Jobs report disk io wait for /var/log/audit-exporter. GPU workload not scheduled until logs shipped.
helen: any errors in exporter logs?
harry: lots of `rate limit exceeded` + `write timeout` to S3. Also saw exporter OOM in one canary (restarted).
opsbot: deploybot: Canary rollout: audit-config-service v2.3.1 -> eu-west-1 COMPLETED at 2025-11-11T14:01:12Z. No automatic rollback.
maya: ok, rollback TTL to 72h for now? cost spike fear but we need stability.
liam: before rollback — can we throttle upstream bounces or increase uploader parallelism? maybe tune `exporter.max_concurrency` to 8.
helen: exporter config is in repo: infra/audit-exporter/config.yaml. Current `max_concurrency: 4`. We can bump to 12 temporarily.
maya: I can patch quick, but we should also reduce sampling rate slightly so backlog doesn't regrow. Suggested: `sampling.rate: 0.8 -> 0.5` (50% of events) and revert TTL to 72h.
harry: sounds good. Plan: 1) increase exporter concurrency to 12, 2) set sampling.rate=0.5, 3) revert ttl to 72h. Apply to eu-west-1 canary now, then watch.
liam: agree. add a short-lived retention override instead of full rollback? TTL patch should be labelled `temp-retention-72h` with expiry in 48h.
maya: deploying patch now. patch diff:
```yaml
# infra/audit-exporter/config.yaml
exporter:
  max_concurrency: 12
sampling:
  rate: 0.5
retention:
  ttl_hours: 72  # temp rollback, expires in 48h via automation
```
helen: creating a quick runbook note in #runbook with rollback steps and alert thresholds.
opsbot: ci: audit-exporter config patch passed lint and integration tests. Promoting to canary.
harry: canary now shows upload queue depth dropping from 18k -> 1.2k after 6m. GPU warmups progressing.
security-bot: alert: retention increase detected in prod audit config. Recording change to compliance log. Ticket: SEC-8812.
liam: good catch. security-bot, add a flag that marks temporary retention overrides in compliance export so we can justify cost.
security-bot: noted. Added tag `temp_retention=true` to SEC-8812 entry.
maya: monitoring: set alert if uploader queue > 5000 for >5m or gpu-warmup-failed > 3 in 10m.
helen: added those alerts. Also scheduled a retrospective tomorrow 11:00 to discuss better autoscaling for exporter and a safer TTL rollout process.
harry: action items: maya revert TTL automation in 48h if no issues (or extend with SEC signoff), liam open PS to allow exporter horizontal autoscaling, helen write runbook, ops to monitor warmups.
liam: I'll open infra-PR and link SEC-8812.
maya: thanks everyone. keeping an eye. :eyes: 
helen: thumbs up. :thumbsup:
opsbot: incidentbot: incident closed (mitigated) — audit-export backlog reduced, GPU warmers resumed. Close after postmortem.
